items.title: 一锦织就世纪工程 平陆运河壮锦长卷首次亮相
items.summary: 9月13日，主创团队、高校学子、留学生代表手持平陆运河壮锦长卷巡游展示。陈冠言 摄 平陆运河壮锦长卷细节。长卷聚焦运河沿线的自然风貌与人文地标，将各族人民共同守护的家园美景尽数织入锦缎。陈冠言 摄 平陆运河壮锦长卷细节。此篇章聚焦工程建设的壮阔壮举，重点刻画马道、企石、青年三大航运枢纽，将建设者的坚守、各族民众的同心协力与工程的磅礴气势，永久定格在锦缎之上，彰显铸牢中华民族共同体意识在工程建设中的生动实践。陈冠言 摄 平陆运河壮锦长卷细节。该部分重点描绘通江达海的壮阔景象，刻画5000吨级货轮经钦州港驶入北部湾的画面，细致展现中国与东盟船只往来繁忙的热闹场景，将壮锦传统的云雷纹、水波纹、太阳纹融入设计，分别化作祥云、运河碧浪与普照大地的阳光，寓意这条世纪之河照亮八桂大地未来，承载着广西各族民众的希望，也承载着中国与东盟携手发展的愿景，生生不息、绵延不绝。陈冠言 摄 柬埔寨留学生上演舞蹈。陈冠言 摄 参观者拍摄平陆运河壮锦长卷。陈冠言 摄

items.title: Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor: the future according to end times fascism – video
items.summary: In a new video, Klein and Taylor outline a ominous evolution taking shape on the far right – and how to stay loyal to this planet and each otherFeatured essay: The end times fascists are plotting their escape from our world. Our mission is clearAn ominous evolution is under way on the far right. It is a dangerous shift that is linked to our era of existential crises, defined by its pandemics, climate emergencies, resource wars and rogue tech. Today’s fascists are part of a dangerous and fractious alliance – from messianic venture capitalists to army-controlling theocrats – united by the belief that the end of the world is upon us and that only a chosen few deserve to be saved. That is the thesis of Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor’s new book, End Times Fascism: And the Fight for the Living World.Since it can be hard to believe that political and corporate leaders would actively give up on our shared future on this singular planet, they also collaborated with film-makers Emma Dessau, Austin Bedell and P Nick Curran to create a video in which we hear directly from many of the people behind this threat – and outline why this is the moment for the rest of us to commit to each other and our shared home. The Guardian is pleased to share it for the first time.End Times Fascism: And the Fight for the Living World is out 15 September via Farrar, Straus and GirouxNaomi Klein is a Guardian US columnist and contributing writer. She is the professor of climate justice and co-director of the Centre for Climate Justice at the University of British ColumbiaAstra Taylor is a writer, organizer and documentary maker and a co-founder of the Debt Collective Continue reading...

items.title: AI will transform capitalism – but how?
items.summary: Technology is going to drastically reshape the economy, and it’s within our power to decide what that looks likeThe idea that autonomous, thinking machines may one day destroy property, hierarchy and inequality is as old as western political thought. In Aristotle’s Politics, the philosopher cites a fantasy from the Iliad, in which machines begin to act independently of human direction, concluding: “If every tool could perform its own work when ordered, or by seeing what to do in advance … if thus shuttles wove and quills played harps of themselves, master-craftsmen would have no need of assistants and masters no need of slaves.”The dream that automation could inaugurate a classless society is also present in the writings of Karl Marx. In 1858 he imagined the replacement of intellectual property with “socialised knowledge”, which would merge into a “general intellect”, blowing the foundations of capitalism sky high. items.title: ‘Trump accounts’ promise to mint child millionaires. Experts have their doubts

But with midterm elections fast approaching and his approval ratings very low, the US president has repeatedly trumpeted a two-month-old program designed to help the nation’s children. That program, unhumbly named “Trump accounts”, calls for the federal government to give a one-time $1,000 seed deposit to every newborn whose family applies.In campaign speeches this summer, Trump has sought to milk these accounts for maximum political advantage, making big promises about how much these accounts will help the nation’s children. In a speech in Las Vegas last month, Trump hailed the program, saying: “It’s really giving [children] a head start on the American dream… They start off with $1,000 … and they can end up with $100,000, $200,000, $300,000” and if the stock market booms, “you’d end up with $1m”. items.title: Spygate saga continues to haunt Southampton as case drags on
items.summary: Manager Tonda Eckert’s future remains in the balance with the FA yet to decide over a suitable punishmentFifty seconds was all it took for the chant to begin. “You know what you are, you know what you are, cheating bastards, you know what you are,” bellowed the Bristol City fans, starting up a cry heard from every away contingent coming to St Mary’s Stadium this season. The Southampton supporters responded with sarcastic applause, then drowned out the noise with songs of their own.This is what life is now like for Southampton after May’s spying scandal – a saga whose full consequences are still unknown and could have ramifications for the season ahead. The English Football League acted swiftly after photographs emerged of a junior staff member hiding behind a tree to film a Middlesbrough training session, expelling Southampton from the Championship play-offs and deducting four points after the club admitted multiple spying offences, including on Oxford United and Ipswich. The Football Association’s case against Tonda Eckert, the manager, is taking far longer. And patience is wearing thin. Continue reading...

items.title: Ben Shelton faces date with destiny against Zverev in US Open final
items.summary: World No 4 will become the first Black American man to win the singles title at Flushing Meadow since Arthur Ashe if he can beat German for the first timeAs Ben Shelton lapped up the explosion of joy and adoration from a full Arthur Ashe Stadium after reaching a grand slam final for the first time, one of his first thoughts was of his paternal grandmother, Regina, who died this year. Shelton credited his grandmother with ensuring that his father, Bryan, made it as a top professional, becoming one of a small group of Black men on the tour. “My dad lost his mom earlier this year and she’s the reason he was able to play tennis,” he said. “Without her, there’s no Ben Shelton standing here today. So this one is for her.”Shelton stands on the verge of history. On Sunday, he will attempt to become the first Black American man to win the US Open singles title since Arthur Ashe in 1968, a feat he will attempt inside the stadium named after Ashe. Shelton would also be the first Black man to win any grand slam singles title since Yannick Noah at Roland Garros in 1983, and the third overall. He is also aiming to become the first American man to win a major singles title since Andy Roddick won the US Open in 2003. Continue reading...
